title: Israel National Cyber Directorate warns of fake Israel Police messages demanding payment of traffic fines
date_note: The page gives only its own publication day; the warning was published that day.
summary: Emess reports that the Israel National Cyber Directorate warns of messages impersonating the Israel Police that are being sent to citizens' phones. They say the recipient has an unpaid traffic ticket and ask for payment through a link, and threaten additional fines if payment is late. The directorate says some include a ticket number, which does not prove a message is genuine.
plain: The Israeli cyber directorate warns of fake police messages that say you owe a traffic fine and push you to pay through a link. A ticket number in the message does not make it genuine, it says.
exec: The directorate, as reported by Emess, warns of fake police payment messages that could lead people to hand over card details.
action: The directorate advises not clicking links in suspicious messages, checking for a ticket on the official gov.il traffic-fine service, and calling your card issuer at once if you entered card details.
impact: Warning only; the page gives no number of recipients or victims.

validation.note: Single publisher (Emess) relaying the directorate's warning; the directorate's own page was not found or read.
